  The patch introduces a real race in the new manual-fail path, and two of the new hardening guards can strand or block otherwise valid review-start/review-analysis flows. Those are correctness issues in supported user paths, so the patch should not be considered correct as-is.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Fence or ignore the active attempt before failing a running review — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts:288-297
  If `/fail` is called while a review is already `running`, this code only flips the row to `failed`; the claimed worker keeps executing. Because `processReviewRun()` still schedules retries and finalizes errors for `review_execution_aborted` runs, any later transient/model failure from that in-flight attempt can turn the review back into `queued` or overwrite the manual-abort reason, so "Fail review" is not reliable for running reviews.

- [P2] Do not abort auto-start after the review has already been created — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts:393-395
  In `auto` mode, `deriveReviewPolicy()` has already created the review before this abort check runs. If the SSE client disconnects or the caller cancels between creation and approval, we throw here and never send the completed payload containing the `reviewId`, leaving a stranded policy-ready review that the caller cannot resume and causing retries from Studio to create duplicates for the same commit.

- [P2] Require cross-file evidence only when a non-changed match actually exists — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts:987-990
  `integrationSearchQueries.length > 0` is only a heuristic from the changed files, not proof that any untouched dependency exists. On self-contained diffs that mention `/recover`, `onEvent`, or similar tokens but whose relevant code is all in changed files, this forces the completion guard to demand a non-changed read that cannot be satisfied, so the review ends as `review_analysis_insufficient_evidence` instead of returning a report.

  <results>
  The new abort handling can strand created reviews during studio startup, and the new manual-fail flow is not actually terminal because the active worker can still retry or overwrite its state afterward. Those are correctness issues in the newly added recovery/startup behavior.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Stop aborting the studio flow after a review has been created — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts:278-281
  `emitEvent()` now re-throws `AbortError` on every later status update, including the updates sent *after* `deriveReviewPolicy()` has already created a review. If the SSE client disconnects in that window, the auto flow exits before `approveReviewPolicy()` runs, leaving a real review stranded in a non-queued state with no review ID returned to the caller; in review mode it similarly creates an orphaned policy review. A transient tab refresh or network drop during startup is enough to trigger this.

- [P1] Keep manual-fail state terminal for the active worker — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts:297-302
  This marks a running review as `failed`, but the in-flight worker is still allowed to continue through `processReviewRun()`'s normal retry/failure handling. If that same attempt later times out or hits another retryable error, the existing runner code can call `scheduleReviewRetry()` and move the review back to `queued`, or overwrite `review_execution_aborted` with `review_execution_failed`. That makes the new `/fail` action non-terminal հենց in the stuck-run scenario it is meant to clean up.
  </results>
  </user_action>

Found:
- The Studio abort finding was stale against the current code. [studio-create.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts) already stops honoring aborts once a review has been created, so post-`deriveReviewPolicy()` disconnects do not strand the review.
- The manual-fail terminal-state finding was also already fixed in the current runner. [review-runner.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner.ts) already re-checks persisted state after execution and before success/retry/failure finalization, so a manually failed running review stays terminal.

Fixed:
- I added explicit Studio regression coverage so this behavior is now directly asserted instead of inferred. The new test helper and assertions are in [studio-create.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts) and [studio-create.test.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/test/app/reviews/studio-create.test.ts).
- I re-verified the worker manual-fail fence through the existing runner regression in [review-runner.test.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/test/lib/review-runner.test.ts). No additional production change was needed there because the terminal-state fix was already present.

Verification:
- `source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 20 >/dev/null && pnpm test -- studio-create`
- `pnpm --filter @dayhaysoos/nimbus-worker test -- review-runner`

Both passed.

<user_action>
  <context>User initiated a review task. Here's the full review output from reviewer model. User may select one or more comments to resolve.</context>
  <action>review</action>
  <results>

payload.message:
Found:
- [review-runner/finalization.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts) was dropping successful output whenever the row was no longer `running`, which meant stale-recovery transitions like `queued`/`retry_scheduled` could discard a valid completion from the original attempt.
- [review-analysis/provider.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis/provider.ts) was not forwarding `reasoningEffort` or `forceComplete` through the Cloudflare-backed provider path, so repair/finalization turns could lose the “must complete now” instruction.

Fixed:
- I changed successful finalization to fence by attempt count instead of `status === 'running'`, and to keep manual-fail terminal. `processReviewRun()` now passes the claimed attempt count into [finalizeSuccessfulReview](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts), so a stale-recovered row from the same attempt can still persist a valid success, but an older attempt still won’t clobber a newer retry.
- I forwarded `reasoningEffort` and `forceComplete` in the Cloudflare provider request body in [provider.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis/provider.ts).
- I added regression coverage for both cases in [review-finalization.test.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/test/lib/review-finalization.test.ts) and [review-analysis-provider.test.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/test/lib/review-analysis-provider.test.ts).

Verification:
- `pnpm --filter @dayhaysoos/nimbus-worker test -- review-finalization`
- `pnpm --filter @dayhaysoos/nimbus-worker test -- review-analysis-provider`

Both passed.

<user_action>
  <context>User initiated a review task. Here's the full review output from reviewer model. User may select one or more comments to resolve.</context>
  <action>review</action>
  <results>
  The new disconnect-driven abort handling can leave partially completed review-startup side effects with no way for the caller to learn the resulting review/workspace IDs. That makes the startup flow incorrect under a real, user-triggered disconnect scenario.

Review comment:

- [P2] Don't abort on SSE close before startup calls are actually cancellable — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/ui-proxy.ts:197-199
  When the browser closes `/api/studio/new-review/start/events`, this new `abortController.abort()` path fires immediately, but the downstream startup work still does not accept that signal. If the disconnect happens while `resolveReviewContext`, `deriveReviewPolicy`, or `approveReviewPolicy` is already in flight, those calls can still create a workspace/deployment or even queue a review, and the next `emitEvent()` then throws `AbortError` before the client ever receives the generated review ID/route. That leaves orphaned startup work the caller cannot discover or resume after a reload.
  </results>
  </user_action>

findings.title: [P2] Don't abort on SSE close before startup calls are actually cancellable
findings.body: When the browser closes `/api/studio/new-review/start/events`, this new `abortController.abort()` path fires immediately, but the downstream startup work still does not accept that signal. If the disconnect happens while `resolveReviewContext`, `deriveReviewPolicy`, or `approveReviewPolicy` is already in flight, those calls can still create a workspace/deployment or even queue a review, and the next `emitEvent()` then throws `AbortError` before the client ever receives the generated review ID/route. That leaves orphaned startup work the caller cannot discover or resume after a reload.

Found:
- The SSE Studio start route in [ui-proxy.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/ui-proxy.ts) was aborting `startStudioNewReview()` as soon as the socket closed, even though the downstream startup work is not actually cancellable. That could leave partial startup side effects with no returned IDs.

Fixed:
- I removed the disconnect-driven abort from the SSE proxy path. Socket close and SSE write failures now only stop streaming; they no longer cancel the underlying startup flow.
- I added a proxy test seam and regression in [ui-proxy.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/ui-proxy.ts) and [ui-proxy.test.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/test/app/reviews/ui-proxy.test.ts) that asserts the streaming route no longer passes a cancellation signal into `startStudioNewReview()`.

Verification:
- `source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 20 >/dev/null && pnpm test -- ui-proxy`
- `source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 20 >/dev/null && pnpm test -- studio-create`

Both passed.

<user_action>
  <context>User initiated a review task. Here's the full review output from reviewer model. User may select one or more comments to resolve.</context>
  <action>review</action>
  <results>
  The patch introduces a non-terminal manual-fail state, can orphan newly created reviews when startup is aborted mid-request, and can force false analysis failures on isolated diffs. Those are functional regressions in user-facing recovery and review startup flows.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Treat manual-fail as terminal for the in-flight attempt — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts:297-301
  When `manuallyFailReviewRun()` marks a running review as `review_execution_aborted`, the original `processReviewRun()` is still free to continue. If that attempt later hits a transient failure such as a provider timeout or D1 lock, the runner's normal catch path will still schedule a retry or overwrite the terminal error, so the new "Fail review" action does not stay failed for the exact stuck-running case it was added to handle.

- [P2] Propagate cancellation once review creation starts — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts:372-378
  If the SSE client disconnects after the pre-check but before `deriveReviewPolicy()` resolves, this await still creates a review on the worker because the abort signal is only checked before the request. The following `emitEvent()` then throws `AbortError`, so the browser never receives `derived.reviewId`; retrying "Start review" creates a second review for the same workspace/deployment because `/api/reviews/policy/derive` is not idempotent.

- [P2] Require cross-file reads only after a cross-file match exists — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts:987-990
  This new evidence gate is turned on whenever `integrationSearchQueries.length > 0`, but those queries come from syntax like `onEvent`, `start*`, or `resolve*` in the changed file, not from proof that a repo-local dependency actually exists. On isolated diffs or symbols imported from external packages, `search_code` can return only the changed file (or nothing), leaving `readCrossFilePaths` empty forever; every `complete` action is then rejected and the review fails with `review_analysis_insufficient_evidence` even though there is no non-changed file to read.
  </results>
  </user_action>

findings.title: [P1] Treat manual-fail as terminal for the in-flight attempt
findings.body: When `manuallyFailReviewRun()` marks a running review as `review_execution_aborted`, the original `processReviewRun()` is still free to continue. If that attempt later hits a transient failure such as a provider timeout or D1 lock, the runner's normal catch path will still schedule a retry or overwrite the terminal error, so the new "Fail review" action does not stay failed for the exact stuck-running case it was added to handle.

findings.title: [P2] Propagate cancellation once review creation starts
findings.body: If the SSE client disconnects after the pre-check but before `deriveReviewPolicy()` resolves, this await still creates a review on the worker because the abort signal is only checked before the request. The following `emitEvent()` then throws `AbortError`, so the browser never receives `derived.reviewId`; retrying "Start review" creates a second review for the same workspace/deployment because `/api/reviews/policy/derive` is not idempotent.

findings.title: [P2] Require cross-file reads only after a cross-file match exists
findings.body: This new evidence gate is turned on whenever `integrationSearchQueries.length > 0`, but those queries come from syntax like `onEvent`, `start*`, or `resolve*` in the changed file, not from proof that a repo-local dependency actually exists. On isolated diffs or symbols imported from external packages, `search_code` can return only the changed file (or nothing), leaving `readCrossFilePaths` empty forever; every `complete` action is then rejected and the review fails with `review_analysis_insufficient_evidence` even though there is no non-changed file to read.

Those are functional regressions in user-facing recovery and review startup flows.

payload.message:
The patch introduces a non-terminal manual-fail state, can orphan newly created reviews when startup is aborted mid-request, and can force false analysis failures on isolated diffs. Those are functional regressions in user-facing recovery and review startup flows.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Treat manual-fail as terminal for the in-flight attempt — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts:297-301
  When `manuallyFailReviewRun()` marks a running review as `review_execution_aborted`, the original `processReviewRun()` is still free to continue. If that attempt later hits a transient failure such as a provider timeout or D1 lock, the runner's normal catch path will still schedule a retry or overwrite the terminal error, so the new "Fail review" action does not stay failed for the exact stuck-running case it was added to handle.

- [P2] Propagate cancellation once review creation starts — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts:372-378
  If the SSE client disconnects after the pre-check but before `deriveReviewPolicy()` resolves, this await still creates a review on the worker because the abort signal is only checked before the request. The following `emitEvent()` then throws `AbortError`, so the browser never receives `derived.reviewId`; retrying "Start review" creates a second review for the same workspace/deployment because `/api/reviews/policy/derive` is not idempotent.

- [P2] Require cross-file reads only after a cross-file match exists — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts:987-990
  This new evidence gate is turned on whenever `integrationSearchQueries.length > 0`, but those queries come from syntax like `onEvent`, `start*`, or `resolve*` in the changed file, not from proof that a repo-local dependency actually exists. On isolated diffs or symbols imported from external packages, `search_code` can return only the changed file (or nothing), leaving `readCrossFilePaths` empty forever; every `complete` action is then rejected and the review fails with `review_analysis_insufficient_evidence` even though there is no non-changed file to read.

  <results>
  The new recovery/startup hardening paths still have abort and manual-fail regressions that can strand reviews or undo an operator's stop request. Those are correctness issues in the newly introduced flows, so the patch should not be considered correct as-is.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Don't abort auto queueing after `deriveReviewPolicy()` succeeds — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts:393-394
  On the SSE startup path, `ui-proxy` aborts `options.signal` as soon as the browser disconnects. If that happens after `deriveReviewPolicy()` has already created `derived.reviewId` but before `approveReviewPolicy()` runs, this guard exits early and leaves the review stuck in its just-created `policy_ready` state instead of queued, so a tab refresh or brief network drop can create orphaned auto-mode reviews that the user never gets routed to.

- [P1] Prevent manual fail from being undone by the running worker — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts:297-302
  For `running` reviews this only updates the row to `failed`; the worker already inside `processReviewRun()` keeps executing. If that in-flight attempt later throws a retryable timeout or network error, the unchanged catch path still calls `scheduleReviewRetry()`, which moves the review back to `queued` and silently undoes the operator's manual stop; even non-retryable failures will overwrite `review_execution_aborted` with a different terminal error.

- [P2] Re-check cancellation before starting workspace deployment — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/context.ts:408-418
  The signal is checked before emitting the `deployment` progress event, but not again after that callback returns. In the SSE flow a disconnect during this event aborts the controller inside the callback, yet we still enter `deployWorkspaceForCommitFlow()` immediately afterward, so closing the page at that moment still launches the full deploy and only aborts after the expensive work has already run.
  </results>

findings.title: [P1] Don't abort auto queueing after `deriveReviewPolicy()` succeeds
findings.body: On the SSE startup path, `ui-proxy` aborts `options.signal` as soon as the browser disconnects. If that happens after `deriveReviewPolicy()` has already created `derived.reviewId` but before `approveReviewPolicy()` runs, this guard exits early and leaves the review stuck in its just-created `policy_ready` state instead of queued, so a tab refresh or brief network drop can create orphaned auto-mode reviews that the user never gets routed to.

findings.title: [P1] Prevent manual fail from being undone by the running worker
findings.body: For `running` reviews this only updates the row to `failed`; the worker already inside `processReviewRun()` keeps executing. If that in-flight attempt later throws a retryable timeout or network error, the unchanged catch path still calls `scheduleReviewRetry()`, which moves the review back to `queued` and silently undoes the operator's manual stop; even non-retryable failures will overwrite `review_execution_aborted` with a different terminal error.

findings.title: [P2] Re-check cancellation before starting workspace deployment
findings.body: The signal is checked before emitting the `deployment` progress event, but not again after that callback returns. In the SSE flow a disconnect during this event aborts the controller inside the callback, yet we still enter `deployWorkspaceForCommitFlow()` immediately afterward, so closing the page at that moment still launches the full deploy and only aborts after the expensive work has already run.

- `PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v20.20.1/bin:$PATH" pnpm test -- studio-create`

<user_action>
  <context>User initiated a review task. Here's the full review output from reviewer model. User may select one or more comments to resolve.</context>
  <action>review</action>
  <results>
  The patch introduces real hardening, but it still leaves stale and manually failed executions insufficiently fenced, and it does not wire the new repair controls through the AGENT_SDK path. Those cases can overwrite or resurrect reviews and prevent the new repair loop from working in one supported deployment mode.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Fence finalization by attempt before accepting recovered output — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts:27-29
  When `recoverStaleRunningReviewIfNeeded()` requeues a slow review, the original worker is still running. This guard only checks `latest.status === 'running'`, so once the replacement attempt is claimed and flips the row back to `running`, the stale original attempt can still persist `succeeded` findings over the newer run; if the retry has not been claimed yet, the same guard drops the finished report entirely. content.text: I want you to do some research for me. I'm trying to build a good quality AI code review tool. codex was able to find bugs with the review command that my tool can't find. codex is open source and their review command seeems to just be a prompt: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/review_prompt.md?plain=1#L4 can you look into how they handle review? Do they do any tool calls or is it just a raw prompt that handles it?

At commit `23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa`, it is not just a raw prompt.

`review_prompt.md` is the review rubric, but the actual `/review` flow creates a separate Codex sub-agent, sets that rubric as `base_instructions`, and runs a normal one-shot agent turn through `run_codex_thread_one_shot(...)`. See [`tasks/review.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/review.rs) and [`codex_delegate.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/codex_delegate.rs).

What that means in practice:

- Output format is prompt-driven, not schema-driven. They pass `final_output_json_schema: None` and then parse the model text back into `ReviewOutputEvent` in [`tasks/review.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/review.rs).
- The diff is not injected as raw patch text. The review request is a short user prompt like “review current changes”, “review commit X”, or “run `git diff <merge-base>`” from [`review_prompts.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/review_prompts.rs).
- A test explicitly checks that the request input contains the environment context plus the raw review prompt, not parent chat history or a precomputed diff: [`core/tests/suite/review.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/tests/suite/review.rs).
- Tooling is still in play. The review sub-agent is a normal Codex thread with inherited managers for skills/plugins/MCP in [`codex_delegate.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/codex_delegate.rs).
- Review-specific restrictions only disable some things like web search/collab and force approval policy to `Never`; they do not reduce review to pure prompt-only reasoning: [`tasks/review.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/review.rs).
- There is even an app-server test showing a review turn can produce a shell command execution/approval item, which is strong evidence that tool calls are part of the design: [`app-server/tests/suite/v2/review.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/app-server/tests/suite/v2/review.rs).

So the short answer is:

It uses a prompt for the review rubric and output contract, but the review command itself is implemented as a real sub-agent workflow with tool access. It is not “just send this markdown prompt and hope.” The agent is expected to inspect the repo itself, often via shell/git, rather than being handed the diff inline.

If you want, I can turn this into a concrete design checklist for your tool: what Codex is doing that likely helps it find bugs your reviewer misses.
tell me more about the subagent. can you find out what tools it uses?

Yes. At that commit, the review subagent is a real child Codex session with normal tool plumbing, not just a prompt-only reviewer.

It is spawned through `run_codex_thread_one_shot(...)`, which calls `Codex::spawn(...)` and inherits the parent session’s `skills_manager`, `plugins_manager`, `mcp_manager`, environment, and exec policy. It does not inject any special review-only dynamic tools. Sources: [review.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/review.rs), [codex_delegate.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/codex_delegate.rs).

What review explicitly changes before spawning:
- It disables `web_search`.
- It disables `Feature::Collab` and `Feature::SpawnCsv`.
- It sets the subagent’s `base_instructions` to `REVIEW_PROMPT`.
- It sets approval policy to `AskForApproval::Never`.
- It does not pass a `final_output_json_schema`; the model output is parsed afterward from text/JSON.
Sources: [review.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/review.rs).

What tools it likely still has in normal `gpt-5-codex` review mode:
- Shell execution: either `shell_command`, or `exec_command` + `write_stdin` in unified-exec mode.
- `update_plan`
- `request_user_input`
- `apply_patch`
- Possibly `view_image`
- MCP/app/plugin tools if those are configured
Sources: [tool_registry_plan.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/tools/src/tool_registry_plan.rs), [spec_tests.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_tests.rs).

What review removes from that default toolset:
- `web_search`
- Collab tools like `spawn_agent`, `send_input`, `resume_agent`, `wait_agent`, `close_agent`
- CSV fanout via `spawn_agents_on_csv`
Sources: [review.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/review.rs), [spec_tests.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_tests.rs).

One nuance: `review.rs` has a comment saying blocked tools include `view image`, but the general tool registry still adds `view_image` whenever an environment exists. I would treat `view_image` as ambiguous at this commit: intended to be blocked, but not obviously removed by the code path I found. Sources: [review.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/review.rs), [tool_registry_plan.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/tools/src/tool_registry_plan.rs).

The important behavioral point is that the reviewer is expected to gather context itself. The review prompt asks it to inspect current changes or run `git diff` against a merge base / commit, and a test confirms the review request contains environment context plus that short review prompt, not an inline diff dump or full parent history. Sources: [review_prompts.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/review_prompts.rs), [core review tests](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/tests/suite/review.rs).

So the short answer is: the review subagent is a normal tool-using Codex child thread, narrowed for review. It is not just “prompt in, findings out.”

If you want, I can turn this into a concrete blueprint for your reviewer: minimum toolset, prompt shape, and why letting the model inspect the repo itself likely improves bug-finding.
So for the most part it's the codex harness itself, there are no tool calls that help fetch code to complete these reviews?

Mostly yes, but with an important caveat.

There does not appear to be a special review-only “code fetching” pipeline. I did not find logic that preloads file contents, injects full diffs, builds embeddings, or runs a dedicated review retrieval step before the model starts. The review path mainly does this:
- spawn a normal Codex child session
- set the review rubric as instructions
- pass a short review task prompt like “review current changes” or “run `git diff <sha>`”
- let the child use the normal harness/tools to inspect the repo itself

Sources: [review.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/review.rs), [review_prompts.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/review_prompts.rs), [review tests](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/tests/suite/review.rs).

So if by “tool calls that help fetch code” you mean special review-specific tools, then no, I don’t see those.

If you mean “does it still use tools to get code context,” then yes:
- the subagent inherits normal shell/exec tooling from the Codex harness
- the review prompt explicitly tells it to inspect changes via git commands
- tests show review can emit command execution / approval events

Sources: [codex_delegate.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/codex_delegate.rs), [tool registry](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/tools/src/tool_registry_plan.rs), [spec tests](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_tests.rs), [app-server review tests](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/app-server/tests/suite/v2/review.rs).

The cleanest summary is: the advantage is probably not a hidden review retrieval system. It’s that the reviewer is a normal repo-aware agent with shell/git access, operating under a review-focused rubric.

okay well right now I'm working with an agent and making tons of changes to this current code base, we added tool calls for review which feels like overkill. inspect the unstaged changes we have right now to get an idea of what we've been doing, let me know if you think this is over engineering or not

**Findings**
- Medium: this has crossed from “add a few review tools” into a second review engine layered on top of the model. The core review loop now has deterministic pre-analysis, step-budgeting, sensitive-path heuristics, cross-file follow-up reads, and multiple completion-rejection paths in [`review-analysis.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts#L49) and [`review-analysis.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts#L588). On top of that, you added bespoke tools like `trace_symbol`, `trace_terms`, and `trace_branches` in [`tools.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis/tools.ts#L10) and [`tools.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis/tools.ts#L221). That is materially more complex than Codex’s approach, which is closer to “normal agent + generic repo inspection.”  
- Medium: the harness is now heavily overfit to one regression family, and the repo’s own experiment log says the extra machinery still does not find the target backend defects. The repeated attempts in [`regressions.md`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/docs/review-quality/regressions.md#L60) through [`regressions.md`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/docs/review-quality/regressions.md#L197) show the system keeps adding deterministic search heuristics, focus rules, and guards, but still misses R-001/R-002 and drifts into UI/SSE findings. That is a strong overengineering signal: complexity is rising faster than review quality.
- Medium: the output contract is becoming too rigid for the value it adds. The prompt now requires `scenarioCoverage` and `scenarioCoverageNotes` for sensitive paths in [`prompt.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis/prompt.ts#L183), and the loop can reject completions for missing coverage, weak notes, missing sensitive-path findings, or uncleared sensitive paths in [`review-analysis.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts#L1108). That may improve auditability, but it also pushes the model to satisfy harness paperwork instead of spending capacity on bug discovery.

**Verdict**
Yes, I think this is overengineered as written.

The issue is not “tool calls are bad.” A small generic toolset is justified for review. `read_file`, `search_code`, and maybe `read_batch` are reasonable. The overengineering starts when the harness tries to pre-solve the review problem with custom tracing tools, deterministic planning, scenario taxonomies, and forced repair/clearance loops.

The parts I would keep:
- one bounded schema-repair turn, because your own log shows it fixed a real failure mode in [`regressions.md`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/docs/review-quality/regressions.md#L81)
- the manual fail / stale-finalization fencing, because that is operationally pragmatic in [`finalization.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts#L21) and [`ReportPage.tsx`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/components/ReportPage.tsx#L993)

The parts I would cut back hard:
- `trace_symbol`
- `trace_terms`
- `trace_branches`
- most of the sensitive-scenario output bookkeeping
- most deterministic pre-analysis beyond “read changed files + one generic search + one cross-file read if needed”

If you want the shortest recommendation: keep tools, but make them generic. Right now you are building a brittle static-analysis harness around the model instead of giving the model a small, high-leverage repo inspection toolkit.
okay, do you think I should revert a lot of this work or what?

The patch introduces real hardening, but it still leaves stale and manually failed executions insufficiently fenced, and it does not wire the new repair controls through the AGENT_SDK path. Those cases can overwrite or resurrect reviews and prevent the new repair loop from working in one supported deployment mode.

- [P1] Fence finalization by attempt before accepting recovered output — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts:27-29
  When `recoverStaleRunningReviewIfNeeded()` requeues a slow review, the original worker is still running. This guard only checks `latest.status === 'running'`, so once the replacement attempt is claimed and flips the row back to `running`, the stale original attempt can still persist `succeeded` findings over the newer run; if the retry has not been claimed yet, the same guard drops the finished report entirely. Finalization needs to be fenced by the attempt that produced the report, not just the current status.

- [P1] Treat manually failed reviews as terminal before retry scheduling — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts:297-302
  This new path marks a still-running review as `failed` with `review_execution_aborted`, but it does not stop the in-flight worker. If that attempt later hits a transient error (for example a provider timeout or network reset), `processReviewRun()` will still call `scheduleReviewRetry()` and move the review back to `queued`, so the new “Fail review” action does not actually stop the run cleanly. The worker needs to recognize `review_execution_aborted` as a terminal fence before retry/finalization logic runs.

- [P2] Send repair flags to AGENT_SDK review requests — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis/provider.ts:339-345
  The hardened repair flow only works if the second provider call tells the remote agent it is a forced-completion repair turn, but the `AGENT_SDK_URL` branch still posts only `prompt`/`model`/`step`/`history`. In self-hosted deployments that use the Cloudflare agent endpoint instead of direct OpenRouter, a schema-invalid first completion is retried as an ordinary step with no `forceComplete` hint, so the new bounded repair behavior (and `REVIEW_REASONING_EFFORT`) is silently ineffective there.

# Escalation Requests

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |
- Logical operators: &&, ||
- Command separators: ;
- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)

Each resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.

Example:

git pull | tee output.txt

This is treated as two command segments:

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

## How to request escalation

IMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:

- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `"require_escalated"`
- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. "Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?"
- Optionally suggest a `prefix_rule` - this will be shown to the user with an option to persist the rule approval for future sessions.

If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with "require_escalated". ALWAYS proceed to use the `justification` parameter - do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.

## When to request escalation

While commands are running inside the sandbox, here are some scenarios that will require escalation outside the sandbox:

- You need to run a command that writes to a directory that requires it (e.g. running tests that write to /var)
- You need to run a GUI app (e.g., open/xdg-open/osascript) to open browsers or files.

When choosing a `prefix_rule`, request one that will allow you to fulfill similar requests from the user in the future without re-requesting escalation. It should be categorical and reasonably scoped to similar capabilities. You should rarely pass the entire command into `prefix_rule`.

  <action>review</action>
  <results>
  The patch introduces at least two functional regressions in review startup/finalization flows and one configuration no-op in the agent provider path. These issues can orphan reviews, discard valid successful results, or silently ignore the new reasoning-effort setting.

Full review comments:

- [P2] Finish auto-start even after the review record already exists — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts:379-394
  If the SSE start stream is aborted after `deriveReviewPolicy()` returns, the later `emitEvent()`/`throwIfAborted()` checks raise before `approveReviewPolicy()` runs. In `policyMode: 'auto'` that leaves behind a real review row that never gets queued for analysis, so a transient disconnect during Studio startup can create an orphaned review instead of a live run.

- [P2] Let retry-scheduled runs persist a late successful result — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts:27-29
  This new fence drops every successful finalization unless the row is still `running`. `recoverStaleRunningReviewIfNeeded()` now flips slow reviews to `queued` with `retry_scheduled` before sending the replay, so if the original attempt finishes successfully before the queued retry is claimed, `finalizeSuccessfulReview()` returns here and discards the valid report. The review stays queued and redoes work even though the first attempt already produced a usable result.

- [P3] Pass reasoningEffort through on AGENT_SDK_URL requests — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis/provider.ts:339-345
  `runWorkspaceDeploymentAgentAnalysis()` now parses `REVIEW_REASONING_EFFORT`, but the Cloudflare agent provider never includes `input.reasoningEffort` in the JSON body it sends to `AGENT_SDK_URL`. On deployments using this provider path, the new reasoning-effort control is therefore a no-op, so the review-quality tuning added in this change does not actually take effect.
  </results>
  </user_action>

  <action>review</action>
  <results>
  The new abort handling can strand workspace/deployment resources after a client disconnect, and the new manual fail path does not actually stop an in-flight review attempt. Those are concrete regressions in the hardening changes.

Full review comments:

- [P2] Stop treating aborts as best-effort progress failures — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/context.ts:124-127
  When the studio start SSE client disconnects, `startStudioNewReview` now signals cancellation by throwing `AbortError` from its `onEvent` bridge. Swallowing every `onProgress` failure here means `resolveReviewContext` ignores that abort and can keep creating/deploying a workspace until `startStudioNewReview` finally notices the cancellation at `review_creation`. In that disconnect scenario, this change leaves behind a deployed workspace with no review record attached and still burns build/deploy capacity.

- [P2] Fence or cancel the active attempt when failing a running review — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts:297-302
  For a running review this endpoint only flips the row to `failed`; it does not cancel or fence the already-claimed worker. `processReviewRun` only checks for `review_execution_aborted` after `executeReviewRun` returns, so the exact “stuck running review” case this button targets will keep consuming provider time and can continue appending lifecycle events after the UI reports that the review was failed. That makes the new `/fail` flow non-terminating for in-flight work.
  </results>

payload.message:
Found:
- The SSE Studio start route in [ui-proxy.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/ui-proxy.ts) was still aborting startup on socket close, which could strand workspace/deployment work after a disconnect.
- The manual-fail path in [recovery.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts) still only flipped the row; it did not cut off an in-flight provider call, so a running review could keep consuming model time after `/fail`.

Fixed:
- I removed disconnect-driven abort propagation from the SSE proxy path in [ui-proxy.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/ui-proxy.ts). Closing the stream now only stops streaming; it no longer cancels underlying review startup.
- I added real manual-fail abort plumbing through the review runner and analysis provider stack in [review-runner.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner.ts), [shared.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/shared.ts), [deployment-report/analysis.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/deployment-report/analysis.ts), [review-analysis.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts), and [provider.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis/provider.ts). A manual fail now aborts active provider requests instead of only fencing after they return.
- I updated regressions in [ui-proxy.test.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/test/app/reviews/ui-proxy.test.ts) and [review-runner.test.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/test/lib/review-runner.test.ts).

Verification:
- `pnpm --filter @dayhaysoos/nimbus-worker test -- review-runner` passed.
- `pnpm test -- ui-proxy` in `packages/cli` showed [ui-proxy.test.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/test/app/reviews/ui-proxy.test.ts) passing; that broader CLI run then hit an unrelated `review.test` `git` `EAGAIN` failure outside this change.

  <results>
  The patch introduces a real state-management bug in the new manual-fail flow, and its new abort/evidence guards can cause duplicate startup side effects or hard review failures on valid inputs. Those issues mean the change is not safe to consider correct as-is.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Fence manual fails from later retry handling — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts:297-302
  If a user clicks **Fail review** while a run is still in flight and that attempt later ends with a timeout/network error, this endpoint only flips the row to `failed` and emits an event; the worker loop is otherwise unchanged. `processReviewRun` will still run its normal error path afterward, which can schedule `retry_scheduled` or overwrite the manual-abort reason, so the new fail action is not stable for running reviews.

- [P2] Propagate aborts into review-creation requests — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts:336-342
  If the Studio SSE client disconnects while `deriveReviewPolicy()` or the later `approveReviewPolicy()` call is already in flight, the new abort handling only notices that *after* the request returns. In that case the worker can still create or queue a review, but `startStudioNewReview` throws `AbortError` before returning the `reviewId`, so retrying from the UI creates duplicate reviews/workspaces even though the first start actually succeeded.

- [P2] Do not require untouched cross-file evidence unconditionally — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts:300-301
  When a diff changes both sides of an integration (or introduces a brand-new callback/API boundary), there may be no relevant non-changed file to read. This new guard still rejects completion unless `readCrossFilePaths` is non-empty whenever `integrationSearchQueries` are present, so otherwise valid reviews can now fail with `review_analysis_insufficient_evidence` even after reading the diff and every changed file.
  </results>
  </user_action>

findings.title: [P2] Propagate aborts into review-creation requests
findings.body: If the Studio SSE client disconnects while `deriveReviewPolicy()` or the later `approveReviewPolicy()` call is already in flight, the new abort handling only notices that *after* the request returns. In that case the worker can still create or queue a review, but `startStudioNewReview` throws `AbortError` before returning the `reviewId`, so retrying from the UI creates duplicate reviews/workspaces even though the first start actually succeeded.

findings.title: [P2] Do not require untouched cross-file evidence unconditionally
findings.body: When a diff changes both sides of an integration (or introduces a brand-new callback/API boundary), there may be no relevant non-changed file to read. This new guard still rejects completion unless `readCrossFilePaths` is non-empty whenever `integrationSearchQueries` are present, so otherwise valid reviews can now fail with `review_analysis_insufficient_evidence` even after reading the diff and every changed file.

The patch introduces a real state-management bug in the new manual-fail flow, and its new abort/evidence guards can cause duplicate startup side effects or hard review failures on valid inputs. Those issues mean the change is not safe to consider correct as-is.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Fence manual fails from later retry handling — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts:297-302
  If a user clicks **Fail review** while a run is still in flight and that attempt later ends with a timeout/network error, this endpoint only flips the row to `failed` and emits an event; the worker loop is otherwise unchanged. `processReviewRun` will still run its normal error path afterward, which can schedule `retry_scheduled` or overwrite the manual-abort reason, so the new fail action is not stable for running reviews.

- [P2] Propagate aborts into review-creation requests — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts:336-342
  If the Studio SSE client disconnects while `deriveReviewPolicy()` or the later `approveReviewPolicy()` call is already in flight, the new abort handling only notices that *after* the request returns. In that case the worker can still create or queue a review, but `startStudioNewReview` throws `AbortError` before returning the `reviewId`, so retrying from the UI creates duplicate reviews/workspaces even though the first start actually succeeded.

- [P2] Do not require untouched cross-file evidence unconditionally — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts:300-301
  When a diff changes both sides of an integration (or introduces a brand-new callback/API boundary), there may be no relevant non-changed file to read. This new guard still rejects completion unless `readCrossFilePaths` is non-empty whenever `integrationSearchQueries` are present, so otherwise valid reviews can now fail with `review_analysis_insufficient_evidence` even after reading the diff and every changed file.

Found:
- The cross-file evidence finding was real. [review-analysis.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts) was still requiring a non-changed-file read whenever integration queries existed, even if `search_code` never found any non-changed match.
- The manual-fail retry finding was stale. [review-runner.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner.ts) already fences manual fails before retry/finalization and aborts active provider work.
- The Studio abort finding was stale. [ui-proxy.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/ui-proxy.ts) no longer passes a disconnect-driven abort signal into `startStudioNewReview`, so the SSE path does not throw away a created `reviewId` after a disconnect.

Fixed:
- I changed the evidence guard in [review-analysis.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts) so cross-file reads are only required when `search_code` actually found a non-changed-file match.
- I updated the regression coverage in [review-analysis.test.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/test/lib/review-analysis.test.ts) to cover both cases:
  - no cross-file match, so no forced non-changed read
  - cross-file match exists, so the non-changed read is still required
- No production code change was needed for the manual-fail or Studio findings because those were already fixed in the current tree.

Verification:
- `pnpm --filter @dayhaysoos/nimbus-worker test -- review-analysis`
- `pnpm --filter @dayhaysoos/nimbus-worker test -- review-runner`

Both passed.

  <results>
  The patch introduces regressions in review lifecycle handling: auto-start can strand created reviews after a client disconnect, manual fail is not durable for running attempts, and retry-scheduled runs can silently drop valid successful completions. These are correctness issues in normal recovery/startup paths, so the patch should not be considered correct as-is.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Keep auto-start queueing after the review has been created — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts:379-393
  If the SSE client disconnects after `deriveReviewPolicy()` succeeds but before `approveReviewPolicy()` runs, `emitEvent()` now throws `AbortError` because `ui-proxy.ts` aborts the signal on socket close. In `policyMode === 'auto'` that exits `startStudioNewReview()` with a real review already created but never approved, so the review is stranded in the policy-ready state instead of being queued.

- [P1] Fence the active attempt when manually failing a running review — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts:297-302
  For `POST /api/reviews/:id/fail` on a running review, this only updates the row to `failed`; it does not stop or fence the worker that is already executing that attempt. If that in-flight worker later hits a retryable error (`fetch failed`, `database is locked`, timeout, etc.), `processReviewRun()` will still schedule `retry_scheduled` and move the manually failed review back to `queued`, so the new fail action is not durable.

- [P2] Allow same-attempt success to finalize from retry-scheduled state — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts:27-29
  This guard discards any successful result from an attempt that was moved from `running` to `queued/retry_scheduled` by stale-run recovery but then actually finishes before the replacement attempt is claimed. In that timing window `finalizeSuccessfulReview()` now returns without persisting findings or status, leaving the review queued and forcing a full rerun (or a permanently stuck queued review if the replacement never starts).

  <action>review</action>
  <results>
  The patch introduces regressions in two user-facing recovery/startup flows and a new evidence gate that can fail otherwise-valid reviews. Those issues mean the change cannot be considered correct as-is.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Ignore client aborts once the review has been derived — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts:379-385
  If the SSE client disconnects after `deriveReviewPolicy()` has already created the review but before this `emitEvent()` runs, `emitEvent()` throws `AbortError` and the function exits before `approveReviewPolicy()` is reached. In auto mode that leaves a real review record stranded in a pre-queue state, so a tab close or proxy drop can create reviews that never start analysis and are not surfaced back to the user.

- [P1] Fence running work before marking a review failed manually — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts:297-302
  This only flips the row to `failed`; it does not stop the already-claimed worker. If the in-flight analysis later hits a transient provider/network error, `processReviewRun()` will still call `scheduleReviewRetry()` and move the review back to `queued`, undoing the manual fail. Any `/fail` request against a running review can therefore resurrect the review instead of stopping it cleanly.

- [P2] Only require a cross-file read after search finds one — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts:300-301
  Any diff that produces `integrationSearchQueries` now requires `readCrossFilePaths.size > 0` even when the deterministic `search_code` calls never find a non-changed file to read. In that case every `complete` is rejected, and once the step budget is exhausted the whole review fails with `review_analysis_insufficient_evidence` despite the model having gathered all available evidence.
  </results>
  </user_action>

findings.title: [P1] Ignore client aborts once the review has been derived
findings.body: If the SSE client disconnects after `deriveReviewPolicy()` has already created the review but before this `emitEvent()` runs, `emitEvent()` throws `AbortError` and the function exits before `approveReviewPolicy()` is reached. In auto mode that leaves a real review record stranded in a pre-queue state, so a tab close or proxy drop can create reviews that never start analysis and are not surfaced back to the user.

findings.title: [P1] Fence running work before marking a review failed manually
findings.body: This only flips the row to `failed`; it does not stop the already-claimed worker. If the in-flight analysis later hits a transient provider/network error, `processReviewRun()` will still call `scheduleReviewRetry()` and move the review back to `queued`, undoing the manual fail. Any `/fail` request against a running review can therefore resurrect the review instead of stopping it cleanly.

findings.title: [P2] Only require a cross-file read after search finds one
findings.body: Any diff that produces `integrationSearchQueries` now requires `readCrossFilePaths.size > 0` even when the deterministic `search_code` calls never find a non-changed file to read. In that case every `complete` is rejected, and once the step budget is exhausted the whole review fails with `review_analysis_insufficient_evidence` despite the model having gathered all available evidence.

  The patch adds useful hardening, but the new manual-fail flow is not wired through the running worker, and the new evidence/startup guards introduce concrete failure modes. Those issues can cause explicitly failed reviews to restart or keep running, and can make otherwise reviewable diffs fail analysis.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Keep manually failed reviews out of retry scheduling — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts:297-302
  Marking a running review as `failed` here does not make that state terminal for the worker loop. If the in-flight attempt later exits through a retryable path (for example a provider timeout or network abort), `processReviewRun()` still runs `shouldRetryReviewError()` and `scheduleReviewRetry()`, which moves the review back to `queued/retry_scheduled`. That means the new `/fail` action can undo itself on the exact stuck-run scenarios it is supposed to handle.

- [P2] Abort the in-flight run when manual fail is requested — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts:297-302
  For reviews that are already `running`, this only flips persisted state; nothing in `processReviewRun()`, provider requests, or sandbox execution observes `review_execution_aborted` and stops work. In practice, using the new fail action while a model call is hung still leaves that expensive run consuming worker/model capacity until it finishes or times out, so the feature does not actually "stop the stuck run cleanly."

- [P1] Only require cross-file reads after a cross-file search hit — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts:987-990
  This now forces `collectMissingEvidenceRequirements()` to demand at least one non-changed file read whenever any integration-style query was extracted from the diff. On single-file or small-repo changes where those searches only hit the changed file(s) — or return no match at all — the guard becomes impossible to satisfy, and analysis fails with `review_analysis_insufficient_evidence` even though the model already inspected all reachable code.

- [P2] Re-throw aborts raised from progress callbacks — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/context.ts:118-121
  The new abortable studio flow routes socket-close cancellation through `onProgress`, but this catch swallows callback failures and the caller does not re-check `options.signal` before starting the current stage's work. If the client disconnects while the `workspace` or `deployment` stage emits its active event, Nimbus still creates the workspace or kicks off the deploy after the stream has already been closed.
  </results>
  </user_action>

findings.title: [P1] Keep manually failed reviews out of retry scheduling
findings.body: Marking a running review as `failed` here does not make that state terminal for the worker loop. If the in-flight attempt later exits through a retryable path (for example a provider timeout or network abort), `processReviewRun()` still runs `shouldRetryReviewError()` and `scheduleReviewRetry()`, which moves the review back to `queued/retry_scheduled`. That means the new `/fail` action can undo itself on the exact stuck-run scenarios it is supposed to handle.

findings.title: [P2] Abort the in-flight run when manual fail is requested
findings.body: For reviews that are already `running`, this only flips persisted state; nothing in `processReviewRun()`, provider requests, or sandbox execution observes `review_execution_aborted` and stops work. In practice, using the new fail action while a model call is hung still leaves that expensive run consuming worker/model capacity until it finishes or times out, so the feature does not actually "stop the stuck run cleanly."

findings.title: [P1] Only require cross-file reads after a cross-file search hit
findings.body: This now forces `collectMissingEvidenceRequirements()` to demand at least one non-changed file read whenever any integration-style query was extracted from the diff. On single-file or small-repo changes where those searches only hit the changed file(s) — or return no match at all — the guard becomes impossible to satisfy, and analysis fails with `review_analysis_insufficient_evidence` even though the model already inspected all reachable code.

findings.title: [P2] Re-throw aborts raised from progress callbacks
findings.body: The new abortable studio flow routes socket-close cancellation through `onProgress`, but this catch swallows callback failures and the caller does not re-check `options.signal` before starting the current stage's work. If the client disconnects while the `workspace` or `deployment` stage emits its active event, Nimbus still creates the workspace or kicks off the deploy after the stream has already been closed.

  <results>
  The patch improves recovery/startup handling, but it introduces one regression that can make some reviews impossible to complete and another race that can undo the new manual-fail action. Those issues affect core review execution, so the patch should not be considered correct as-is.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Drop the impossible cross-file evidence requirement — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts:319-320
  For single-file diffs that merely expose an integration-shaped token (for example `onProgress`, `onEvent`, or a static `/api/...` route), `extractIntegrationSearchQueries()` now makes `requiresCrossFileIntegrationEvidence` true even when every relevant match is already in the changed file set. In that case this guard can never be satisfied, so the agent burns through its remaining steps and the review fails with `review_analysis_insufficient_evidence` instead of producing findings.

- [P2] Make success finalization conditional on the row still being running — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts:40-42
  If someone uses the new manual-fail action after this initial status read but before the writes below complete, `finalizeSuccessfulReview()` still persists findings and flips the review back to `succeeded` because those updates are unconditional. That race makes the new fail flow unreliable in the exact “stuck run finally returns” window and can emit a contradictory `review_succeeded` sequence after the operator explicitly aborted the run.

  For single-file diffs that merely expose an integration-shaped token (for example `onProgress`, `onEvent`, or a static `/api/...` route), `extractIntegrationSearchQueries()` now makes `requiresCrossFileIntegrationEvidence` true even when every relevant match is already in the changed file set. In that case this guard can never be satisfied, so the agent burns through its remaining steps and the review fails with `review_analysis_insufficient_evidence` instead of producing findings.

- [P2] Make success finalization conditional on the row still being running — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts:40-42
  If someone uses the new manual-fail action after this initial status read but before the writes below complete, `finalizeSuccessfulReview()` still persists findings and flips the review back to `succeeded` because those updates are unconditional. That race makes the new fail flow unreliable in the exact “stuck run finally returns” window and can emit a contradictory `review_succeeded` sequence after the operator explicitly aborted the run.

Found:
- The cross-file evidence finding was real. [review-analysis.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts) had regressed back to requiring a non-changed-file read whenever integration queries existed, even if search never found any non-changed match.
- The successful-finalization race was real. [finalization.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts) could still flip a review to `succeeded` after a late manual fail if that fail happened after the initial status read.

Fixed:
- I restored the evidence gate in [review-analysis.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts) so cross-file reads are only required when `search_code` actually found a non-changed-file match.
- I made successful finalization’s status write conditional in [finalization.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts), fenced by current eligible state and `expectedAttemptCount`, so a late manual fail can no longer be overwritten by `review_succeeded`.
- I updated regressions in [review-analysis.test.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/test/lib/review-analysis.test.ts) and [review-finalization.test.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/test/lib/review-finalization.test.ts).

Verification:
- `pnpm --filter @dayhaysoos/nimbus-worker test -- review-analysis`
- `pnpm --filter @dayhaysoos/nimbus-worker test -- review-finalization`

Both passed.

  <action>review</action>
  <results>
  The patch introduces multiple correctness regressions in the new recovery/startup logic. Manual fail is not terminal, auto-start can orphan reviews on disconnect, some review analyses now fail due to impossible evidence requirements, and stale-recovered attempts can drop valid successful results.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Preserve manual-fail as a terminal state — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts:297-302
  When the new `/fail` path is used on a `running` review, this only flips the row to `failed`; the in-flight worker is still free to hit the retry/failure paths in `processReviewRun()`. If that attempt later throws a retryable error (for example a provider timeout or network failure), `scheduleReviewRetry()` will move the review back to `queued`, and even non-retryable failures will overwrite the `review_execution_aborted` reason. That means the new “Fail review” control does not reliably stop the stuck run it was added for.

- [P1] Allow stale-recovered attempts to persist success before a retry claims — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts:27-29
  The new `latest.status !== 'running'` guard drops any completion that arrives after `recoverStaleRunningReviewIfNeeded()` has requeued the review as `queued/retry_scheduled`. In the race where attempt 1 finishes successfully after the row is requeued but before attempt 2 is claimed, Nimbus now discards a valid report and leaves the review queued for duplicate analysis. This needs an attempt-count/CAS check, not a blanket rejection of every non-`running` state.

- [P2] Don't strand auto-started reviews on client disconnects — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts:393-395
  In auto mode the review record already exists once `deriveReviewPolicy()` returns, but the new abort check immediately before `approveReviewPolicy()` can still throw if the SSE client disconnects in that window. That leaves a freshly created review stuck in `policy_ready` even though the user asked Nimbus to auto-start analysis, so transient tab closes/network drops now orphan reviews until someone recovers them manually.

- [P2] Only require cross-file reads when search actually found one — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts:300-301
  This new evidence rule makes a cross-file read mandatory whenever `extractIntegrationSearchQueries()` emits any heuristic query, even if every search result stays inside the changed files or finds nothing. Self-contained diffs that merely mention `/api/...`, `onEvent`, `onProgress`, etc. can therefore fail with `review_analysis_insufficient_evidence` despite reading all relevant changed code, because `readCrossFilePaths` can never become non-empty. Gate this requirement on finding a non-changed match first.

findings.title: [P1] Preserve manual-fail as a terminal state
findings.body: When the new `/fail` path is used on a `running` review, this only flips the row to `failed`; the in-flight worker is still free to hit the retry/failure paths in `processReviewRun()`. If that attempt later throws a retryable error (for example a provider timeout or network failure), `scheduleReviewRetry()` will move the review back to `queued`, and even non-retryable failures will overwrite the `review_execution_aborted` reason. That means the new “Fail review” control does not reliably stop the stuck run it was added for.

findings.title: [P1] Allow stale-recovered attempts to persist success before a retry claims
findings.body: The new `latest.status !== 'running'` guard drops any completion that arrives after `recoverStaleRunningReviewIfNeeded()` has requeued the review as `queued/retry_scheduled`. In the race where attempt 1 finishes successfully after the row is requeued but before attempt 2 is claimed, Nimbus now discards a valid report and leaves the review queued for duplicate analysis. This needs an attempt-count/CAS check, not a blanket rejection of every non-`running` state.

findings.title: [P2] Don't strand auto-started reviews on client disconnects
findings.body: In auto mode the review record already exists once `deriveReviewPolicy()` returns, but the new abort check immediately before `approveReviewPolicy()` can still throw if the SSE client disconnects in that window. That leaves a freshly created review stuck in `policy_ready` even though the user asked Nimbus to auto-start analysis, so transient tab closes/network drops now orphan reviews until someone recovers them manually.

findings.title: [P2] Only require cross-file reads when search actually found one
findings.body: This new evidence rule makes a cross-file read mandatory whenever `extractIntegrationSearchQueries()` emits any heuristic query, even if every search result stays inside the changed files or finds nothing. Self-contained diffs that merely mention `/api/...`, `onEvent`, `onProgress`, etc. can therefore fail with `review_analysis_insufficient_evidence` despite reading all relevant changed code, because `readCrossFilePaths` can never become non-empty. Gate this requirement on finding a non-changed match first.

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

The `request_user_input` tool is unavailable in Default mode. If you call it while in Default mode, it will return an error.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. If you absolutely must ask a question because the answer cannot be discovered from local context and a reasonable assumption would be risky, ask the user directly with a concise plain-text question. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.

The patch improves several recovery paths, but it still leaves a race that can corrupt persisted findings and an abort hole that can create reviews after the Studio client disconnects. Those are correctness issues in the new hardening logic.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Guard finding writes behind the current-attempt CAS — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts:105-106
  When a stale attempt finishes after a retry has been scheduled, this function now writes `review_findings` before it knows whether that attempt is still allowed to win. If another worker claims the queued retry (or a manual fail lands) between the initial `getReviewRun()` and `persistSuccessfulReviewStatusIfCurrent()`, the status update correctly affects 0 rows, but the stale attempt has already deleted/reinserted findings for the review. That can leave the live run with findings from the wrong attempt even though its status transition was rejected.

  If the Studio client disconnects while `deployWorkspaceForCommitFlow()` is in flight, `options.signal` becomes aborted during the await, but there is no explicit abort check afterward. In that case `startStudioNewReview()` will continue on to review creation even though the caller disconnected before review creation completed.

payload.message:
Found:
- The stale-attempt findings race was real. [finalization.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts) was still replacing `review_findings` before the success CAS, so a losing attempt could rewrite findings even if its status transition was rejected.
- The post-deploy abort hole was real. [context.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/context.ts) did not re-check `options.signal` after `deployWorkspaceForCommitFlow()` returned, so a disconnect during deployment could still flow into review creation.

Fixed:
- I moved finding persistence behind the success CAS in [finalization.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts), so a stale/manual-failed attempt now exits before touching `review_findings` if it can’t win the conditional status update.
- I added an explicit abort re-check immediately after the deployment await in [context.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/context.ts), so disconnects during deployment stop the flow before review creation.
- I updated regressions in [review-finalization.test.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/test/lib/review-finalization.test.ts) and [studio-create.test.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/test/app/reviews/studio-create.test.ts).

Verification:
- `pnpm --filter @dayhaysoos/nimbus-worker test -- review-finalization`
- `source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 20 >/dev/null && pnpm test -- studio-create` in `packages/cli`

Both passed.

  <action>review</action>
  <results>
  The patch adds useful recovery hardening, but the new abort path can leak unattached startup artifacts and the new manual-fail state is still vulnerable to being overwritten by the runner's catch path. Those are functional regressions in the new recovery/startup behavior.

Full review comments:

- [P2] Clean up created deployment when studio start aborts — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/context.ts:450-450
  If the browser disconnects while `deployWorkspaceForCommitFlow()` is in flight, the new abort handling only notices it here, after the deployment has already been created. `startStudioNewReview()` then treats the request as aborted and exits before `deriveReviewPolicy()`, so the user gets no review ID while Nimbus leaves behind an unattached workspace/deployment with no cleanup path.
