content.text: I want you to do some research for me. I'm trying to build a good quality AI code review tool. codex was able to find bugs with the review command that my tool can't find. codex is open source and their review command seeems to just be a prompt: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/review_prompt.md?plain=1#L4 can you look into how they handle review? Do they do any tool calls or is it just a raw prompt that handles it?

At commit `23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa`, it is not just a raw prompt.

`review_prompt.md` is the review rubric, but the actual `/review` flow creates a separate Codex sub-agent, sets that rubric as `base_instructions`, and runs a normal one-shot agent turn through `run_codex_thread_one_shot(...)`. See [`tasks/review.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/review.rs) and [`codex_delegate.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/codex_delegate.rs).

What that means in practice:

- Output format is prompt-driven, not schema-driven. They pass `final_output_json_schema: None` and then parse the model text back into `ReviewOutputEvent` in [`tasks/review.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/review.rs).
- The diff is not injected as raw patch text. The review request is a short user prompt like “review current changes”, “review commit X”, or “run `git diff <merge-base>`” from [`review_prompts.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/review_prompts.rs).
- A test explicitly checks that the request input contains the environment context plus the raw review prompt, not parent chat history or a precomputed diff: [`core/tests/suite/review.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/tests/suite/review.rs).
- Tooling is still in play. The review sub-agent is a normal Codex thread with inherited managers for skills/plugins/MCP in [`codex_delegate.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/codex_delegate.rs).
- Review-specific restrictions only disable some things like web search/collab and force approval policy to `Never`; they do not reduce review to pure prompt-only reasoning: [`tasks/review.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/review.rs).
- There is even an app-server test showing a review turn can produce a shell command execution/approval item, which is strong evidence that tool calls are part of the design: [`app-server/tests/suite/v2/review.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/app-server/tests/suite/v2/review.rs).

So the short answer is:

It uses a prompt for the review rubric and output contract, but the review command itself is implemented as a real sub-agent workflow with tool access. It is not “just send this markdown prompt and hope.” The agent is expected to inspect the repo itself, often via shell/git, rather than being handed the diff inline.

If you want, I can turn this into a concrete design checklist for your tool: what Codex is doing that likely helps it find bugs your reviewer misses.
tell me more about the subagent. can you find out what tools it uses?

Yes. At that commit, the review subagent is a real child Codex session with normal tool plumbing, not just a prompt-only reviewer.

It is spawned through `run_codex_thread_one_shot(...)`, which calls `Codex::spawn(...)` and inherits the parent session’s `skills_manager`, `plugins_manager`, `mcp_manager`, environment, and exec policy. It does not inject any special review-only dynamic tools. Sources: [review.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/review.rs), [codex_delegate.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/codex_delegate.rs).

What review explicitly changes before spawning:
- It disables `web_search`.
- It disables `Feature::Collab` and `Feature::SpawnCsv`.
- It sets the subagent’s `base_instructions` to `REVIEW_PROMPT`.
- It sets approval policy to `AskForApproval::Never`.
- It does not pass a `final_output_json_schema`; the model output is parsed afterward from text/JSON.
Sources: [review.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/review.rs).

What tools it likely still has in normal `gpt-5-codex` review mode:
- Shell execution: either `shell_command`, or `exec_command` + `write_stdin` in unified-exec mode.
- `update_plan`
- `request_user_input`
- `apply_patch`
- Possibly `view_image`
- MCP/app/plugin tools if those are configured
Sources: [tool_registry_plan.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/tools/src/tool_registry_plan.rs), [spec_tests.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_tests.rs).

What review removes from that default toolset:
- `web_search`
- Collab tools like `spawn_agent`, `send_input`, `resume_agent`, `wait_agent`, `close_agent`
- CSV fanout via `spawn_agents_on_csv`
Sources: [review.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/review.rs), [spec_tests.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_tests.rs).

One nuance: `review.rs` has a comment saying blocked tools include `view image`, but the general tool registry still adds `view_image` whenever an environment exists. I would treat `view_image` as ambiguous at this commit: intended to be blocked, but not obviously removed by the code path I found. Sources: [review.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/review.rs), [tool_registry_plan.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/tools/src/tool_registry_plan.rs).

The important behavioral point is that the reviewer is expected to gather context itself. The review prompt asks it to inspect current changes or run `git diff` against a merge base / commit, and a test confirms the review request contains environment context plus that short review prompt, not an inline diff dump or full parent history. Sources: [review_prompts.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/review_prompts.rs), [core review tests](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/tests/suite/review.rs).

So the short answer is: the review subagent is a normal tool-using Codex child thread, narrowed for review. It is not just “prompt in, findings out.”

If you want, I can turn this into a concrete blueprint for your reviewer: minimum toolset, prompt shape, and why letting the model inspect the repo itself likely improves bug-finding.
So for the most part it's the codex harness itself, there are no tool calls that help fetch code to complete these reviews?

Mostly yes, but with an important caveat.

There does not appear to be a special review-only “code fetching” pipeline. I did not find logic that preloads file contents, injects full diffs, builds embeddings, or runs a dedicated review retrieval step before the model starts. The review path mainly does this:
- spawn a normal Codex child session
- set the review rubric as instructions
- pass a short review task prompt like “review current changes” or “run `git diff <sha>`”
- let the child use the normal harness/tools to inspect the repo itself

Sources: [review.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tasks/review.rs), [review_prompts.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/review_prompts.rs), [review tests](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/tests/suite/review.rs).

So if by “tool calls that help fetch code” you mean special review-specific tools, then no, I don’t see those.

If you mean “does it still use tools to get code context,” then yes:
- the subagent inherits normal shell/exec tooling from the Codex harness
- the review prompt explicitly tells it to inspect changes via git commands
- tests show review can emit command execution / approval events

Sources: [codex_delegate.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/codex_delegate.rs), [tool registry](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/tools/src/tool_registry_plan.rs), [spec tests](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_tests.rs), [app-server review tests](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/23f4cd8459bcc254b4f6f10456f5a12a3eb4faaa/codex-rs/app-server/tests/suite/v2/review.rs).

The cleanest summary is: the advantage is probably not a hidden review retrieval system. It’s that the reviewer is a normal repo-aware agent with shell/git access, operating under a review-focused rubric.

okay well right now I'm working with an agent and making tons of changes to this current code base, we added tool calls for review which feels like overkill. inspect the unstaged changes we have right now to get an idea of what we've been doing, let me know if you think this is over engineering or not

**Findings**
- Medium: this has crossed from “add a few review tools” into a second review engine layered on top of the model. The core review loop now has deterministic pre-analysis, step-budgeting, sensitive-path heuristics, cross-file follow-up reads, and multiple completion-rejection paths in [`review-analysis.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts#L49) and [`review-analysis.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts#L588). On top of that, you added bespoke tools like `trace_symbol`, `trace_terms`, and `trace_branches` in [`tools.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis/tools.ts#L10) and [`tools.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis/tools.ts#L221). That is materially more complex than Codex’s approach, which is closer to “normal agent + generic repo inspection.”  
- Medium: the harness is now heavily overfit to one regression family, and the repo’s own experiment log says the extra machinery still does not find the target backend defects. The repeated attempts in [`regressions.md`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/docs/review-quality/regressions.md#L60) through [`regressions.md`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/docs/review-quality/regressions.md#L197) show the system keeps adding deterministic search heuristics, focus rules, and guards, but still misses R-001/R-002 and drifts into UI/SSE findings. That is a strong overengineering signal: complexity is rising faster than review quality.
- Medium: the output contract is becoming too rigid for the value it adds. The prompt now requires `scenarioCoverage` and `scenarioCoverageNotes` for sensitive paths in [`prompt.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis/prompt.ts#L183), and the loop can reject completions for missing coverage, weak notes, missing sensitive-path findings, or uncleared sensitive paths in [`review-analysis.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts#L1108). That may improve auditability, but it also pushes the model to satisfy harness paperwork instead of spending capacity on bug discovery.

**Verdict**
Yes, I think this is overengineered as written.

The issue is not “tool calls are bad.” A small generic toolset is justified for review. `read_file`, `search_code`, and maybe `read_batch` are reasonable. The overengineering starts when the harness tries to pre-solve the review problem with custom tracing tools, deterministic planning, scenario taxonomies, and forced repair/clearance loops.

The parts I would keep:
- one bounded schema-repair turn, because your own log shows it fixed a real failure mode in [`regressions.md`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/docs/review-quality/regressions.md#L81)
- the manual fail / stale-finalization fencing, because that is operationally pragmatic in [`finalization.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts#L21) and [`ReportPage.tsx`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/components/ReportPage.tsx#L993)

The parts I would cut back hard:
- `trace_symbol`
- `trace_terms`
- `trace_branches`
- most of the sensitive-scenario output bookkeeping
- most deterministic pre-analysis beyond “read changed files + one generic search + one cross-file read if needed”

If you want the shortest recommendation: keep tools, but make them generic. Right now you are building a brittle static-analysis harness around the model instead of giving the model a small, high-leverage repo inspection toolkit.
okay, do you think I should revert a lot of this work or what?

I would not hard-revert everything. I would split it into three buckets.

Keep:
- The bounded repair turn for schema-invalid completions in [`review-analysis.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts#L1287). That addresses a real failure mode instead of adding speculative capability.
- The stale-finalization guard in [`finalization.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts#L21). That is operationally correct and low-risk.
- The manual fail path and UI support in [`recovery.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts#L279), [`query.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/query.ts#L180), and [`ReportPage.tsx`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/components/ReportPage.tsx#L993). That is product/runtime hygiene, not overengineering.

Trim hard:
- Most of the deterministic evidence collector in [`review-analysis.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts#L588).
- The bespoke tracing tools in [`tools.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis/tools.ts#L221).
- The required `scenarioCoverage` / `scenarioCoverageNotes` contract in [`prompt.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis/prompt.ts#L183) and the rejection logic in [`review-analysis.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts#L1108).

So my recommendation is: do a selective rollback, not a blanket revert.

Concretely, I’d aim for this simpler shape:
- Prompt strongly biases toward changed sensitive paths.
- Tools limited to `read_file`, `search_code`, maybe `read_batch`, plus `diff_summary`.
- One repair turn if output shape is bad.
- No custom scenario bookkeeping, no trace-specific tools, no heavy deterministic pre-pass.

If you want, I can make that reduction for you directly as the next step: preserve the good operational changes, remove the overfit review harness pieces, and leave you with a cleaner baseline to test.
yeah make those changes for me please. Deploy to the worker when you're done.

I kept the bounded schema-repair turn, reasoning-effort support, the stale-finalization guard in [finalization.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts), and the manual fail/recovery operational path you already added. The main rollback is in [review-analysis.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts), [tools.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis/tools.ts), [prompt.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis/prompt.ts), and [provider.ts](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis/provider.ts).

okay so here's my problem. Codex found these two bugs in my code base on the last commit: 
• Yes.

  1. Recover review is shown for queued/live states, but the backend recovery API cannot handle normal queued
     reviews, so clicking it can produce a hard error instead of a valid action.

  - File: packages/report-ui/src/components/ReportPage.tsx:964

  2. The SSE review-start flow awaits progress callbacks, so a socket write failure or client disconnect during
     early progress emission can abort workspace creation/deployment and fail review startup.

  - Files:
      - packages/cli/src/app/reviews/ui-proxy.ts:154
      - packages/cli/src/app/reviews/context.ts:72

 I want this review tool to identify those same bugs. I've made tons of changes trying to catch them, however, I haven't been able to. What do you think needs to be done?

What needs to change is not “more tools.” It’s better cross-file contract review.

These two bugs share the same shape:

- Bug 1 is a UI/backend contract mismatch.
  - The UI offers recover in [`ReportPage.tsx`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/components/ReportPage.tsx#L967).
  - The backend rejects recovery for running reviews and only actually supports queued recovery in [`recovery.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts#L201) and [`recovery.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts#L205).
- Bug 2 is a callback-on-critical-path bug.
  - SSE start awaits `startStudioNewReview(... onEvent ...)` in [`ui-proxy.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/ui-proxy.ts#L206).
  - `startStudioNewReview` forwards that into `resolveReviewContext(... onProgress ...)` in [`studio-create.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts#L290).
  - `resolveReviewContext` actually `await`s the progress callback in [`context.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/context.ts#L113).

Your current harness is still weak at exactly that kind of reasoning. It is good at “inspect changed files,” but weak at “follow one integration boundary and verify the callee contract.”

What I think you should do:

1. Make one-hop contract reads mandatory for certain signals.
- If a changed file does `fetch('/api/...')`, deterministically read the matching handler/callee file before allowing completion.
- If a changed file passes or accepts callbacks like `onProgress`, `onEvent`, `onStatus`, deterministically read the callee/emitter chain one hop deeper.
- If a changed file branches on runtime state like `review.status`, deterministically read the server-side state transition handler.

2. Stop relying on “sensitive path” heuristics as the main steering mechanism.
- These misses are in `report-ui` and `cli`, which your old sensitive-path heuristics would naturally underweight.
- The better signal is integration shape, not filename keywords.

3. Add explicit prompt rules for these defect classes.
- “When UI exposes an action, verify the backend accepts that action for the same states.”
- “When optional progress/logging/streaming callbacks are awaited, check whether callback failure can abort the primary operation.”
- “Prefer cross-file contract bugs over local polish findings when the changed code calls APIs or forwards callbacks.”

4. Keep the toolset small.
- `read_file`
- `read_batch`
- `search_code`
- `diff_summary`
That is enough. The problem is retrieval policy, not missing trace tools.

5. Add these two bugs as regression fixtures and score for them directly.
- You already have a regression doc workflow. Use that, but specifically track:
  - `ui_action_backend_state_mismatch`
  - `observability_callback_on_critical_path`

The practical version of the retrieval policy I’d implement is:

- For every changed file:
  - Read the file directly.
  - Extract:
    - imported symbols
    - callback names passed/received
    - fetch/API paths
    - state fields used in gating logic
- Then do at most 2 deterministic follow-ups:

Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `workspace-write`: The sandbox permits reading files, and editing files in `cwd` and `writable_roots`. Editing files in other directories requires approval. Network access is restricted.
# Escalation Requests

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |
- Logical operators: &&, ||
- Command separators: ;
- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)

Each resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.

Example:

git pull | tee output.txt

This is treated as two command segments:

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

## How to request escalation

IMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:

- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `"require_escalated"`
- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. "Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?"
- Optionally suggest a `prefix_rule` - this will be shown to the user with an option to persist the rule approval for future sessions.

If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with "require_escalated". ALWAYS proceed to use the `justification` parameter - do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.

## When to request escalation

While commands are running inside the sandbox, here are some scenarios that will require escalation outside the sandbox:

- You need to run a command that writes to a directory that requires it (e.g. running tests that write to /var)
- You need to run a GUI app (e.g., open/xdg-open/osascript) to open browsers or files.
- If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with `require_escalated`. ALWAYS proceed to use the `sandbox_permissions` and `justification` parameters. do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.
- You are about to take a potentially destructive action such as an `rm` or `git reset` that the user did not explicitly ask for.
- Be judicious with escalating, but if completing the user's request requires it, you should do so - don't try and circumvent approvals by using other tools.

## prefix_rule guidance

When choosing a `prefix_rule`, request one that will allow you to fulfill similar requests from the user in the future without re-requesting escalation. It should be categorical and reasonably scoped to similar capabilities. You should rarely pass the entire command into `prefix_rule`.

### Banned prefix_rules 
Avoid requesting overly broad prefixes that the user would be ill-advised to approve. For example, do not request ["python3"], ["python", "-"], or other similar prefixes that would allow arbitrary scripting.
NEVER provide a prefix_rule argument for destructive commands like rm.
NEVER provide a prefix_rule if your command uses a heredoc or herestring. 

### Examples
Good examples of prefixes:
- ["npm", "run", "dev"]
- ["gh", "pr", "check"]
- ["cargo", "test"]

- I moved the Studio abort boundary in [`context.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/context.ts) so once deployment succeeds, the flow finishes attaching that deployment to a review instead of aborting and leaving unattached resources behind.

  <results>
  The patch introduces a real race in the new manual-fail path that can overwrite a concurrently succeeded review, and the new abort handling can strand created workspace/deployment artifacts when startup is interrupted late. Those are correctness issues, so the patch should not be considered correct as-is.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Guard manual fail against concurrent terminal transitions — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts:297-302
  If `/api/reviews/:id/fail` is called while a run is still `running`, there is a race between the initial `getReviewRun()` check and this unconditional `updateReviewRunStatus()`: a review that finishes successfully in that window will still be downgraded to `failed` here, and its persisted report/summary will be cleared. This needs the same kind of compare-and-set guard used elsewhere for retry/finalization so manual fail only wins when the review is still in the expected state.

- [P2] Don’t abort after context setup has already created startup artifacts — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts:328-340
  If the start-events SSE client disconnects during workspace/deployment setup, `resolveReviewContext()` can still return with a created workspace/deployment, but this post-setup abort path stops before `deriveReviewPolicy()` attaches them to a review. In that case users who navigate away late in startup leave behind unattached review artifacts instead of either finishing the review creation handoff or cleaning up.
  </results>
  </user_action>

payload.message:
Found:
- The manual-fail race was real. [`recovery.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts) was still doing an unconditional terminal write after a stale `getReviewRun()` read, so it could overwrite a concurrently succeeded review.
- The Studio startup abort finding was real. [`studio-create.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts) could still abort after [`resolveReviewContext()`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/context.ts) had already created workspace/deployment artifacts, leaving them unattached to any review.

Fixed:
- I changed manual fail in [`recovery.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts) to use a compare-and-set update keyed to the observed status, with `attempt_count` fencing for `running`. If the review already transitioned, manual fail no longer clears or downgrades it, and it only emits `review_failed` when the CAS wins.
- I moved the Studio abort boundary in [`studio-create.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts) so once context setup returns with a workspace/deployment, the flow always finishes attaching those artifacts to a review instead of aborting mid-handoff.
- I added a recovery API regression in [`reviews.test.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/test/api/reviews.test.ts) covering the concurrent-success manual-fail case.

Verification:
- `pnpm --filter @dayhaysoos/nimbus-worker test -- api/reviews`
- `source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 20 >/dev/null && pnpm test -- studio-create` in `packages/cli`

Both passed.

<user_action>
  <context>User initiated a review task. Here's the full review output from reviewer model. User may select one or more comments to resolve.</context>
  <action>review</action>
  <results>
  The new startup cancellation paths can now strand persisted workspaces, deployments, or reviews in partially created states, and the fail-review UI can report success when the fail request lost a race. Those are concrete correctness issues in the introduced recovery/startup logic.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Stop aborting after deployment setup has already finished — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts:323-323
  If the SSE client disconnects after `resolveReviewContext()` returns, this `emitEvent()` still consults `signal.aborted` and throws before `deriveReviewPolicy()` runs. At that point the workspace and deployment already exist, so the new abort path leaves startup artifacts unattached to any review; in auto mode the later `throwIfAborted()` before `approveReviewPolicy()` can also strand a just-created review in an unqueued state.

- [P2] Clean up created workspaces when startup is aborted mid-flow — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/context.ts:408-408
  When cancellation lands after `createWorkspaceForCommitFlow()` succeeds but before deployment begins, this new abort check exits `resolveReviewContext()` without deleting `workspaceId`. Because the UI proxy now wires browser disconnects into this signal, ordinary cancelled start requests can accumulate unattached workspaces until someone destroys them manually.

- [P3] Base the fail-review toast on the returned review state — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/components/ReportPage.tsx:1012-1014
  The fail endpoint can race with natural completion and return `200` with the latest review already `succeeded` (the worker tests added in this patch cover that case). This handler always shows `Review failed cleanly`, so operators get the opposite outcome from what actually happened. Key the toast off the returned review status or server action instead of assuming the fail won.
  </results>
  </user_action>

<user_action>
  <context>User initiated a review task. Here's the full review output from reviewer model. User may select one or more comments to resolve.</context>
  <action>review</action>
  <results>
  The patch introduces one review-analysis guard that can make some reviews impossible to complete, plus two race/abort issues around the new startup and manual-fail flows. Those regressions can cause failed or orphaned review runs in real usage.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Don't require a cross-file read when search found no cross-file match — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts:300-301
  This now requires a non-changed-file read whenever `integrationSearchQueries.length > 0`, even if every `search_code` hit points back to the changed file or there is no cross-file match at all. Because `runDeterministicEvidenceCollection()` skips changed-path matches when building follow-up reads, diffs that only introduce local callbacks/routes like the new `onProgress`/`onEvent` code can never satisfy this guard and the run fails with `review_analysis_insufficient_evidence` instead of producing a review.

- [P2] Finish auto-start once the review has been created — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts:393-395
  The UI proxy aborts this signal as soon as the SSE client disconnects. In auto mode, if that happens after `deriveReviewPolicy()` has already created the review but before `approveReviewPolicy()` runs, this check throws and leaves a hidden `policy_ready` review behind even though the user asked for an auto-queued run. Since the connection is already gone, the client never receives the `reviewId` needed to resume it, so the start appears to vanish.

- [P1] Fence manual fail so retries cannot resurrect the review — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts:297-302
  This new path only flips the row to `failed`; it does not abort or fence the active runner. If the still-running attempt later exits through a retryable path (for example a provider timeout or transient fetch failure), `processReviewRun()` still calls `scheduleReviewRetry()` and moves the same review back to `queued` with `retry_scheduled`, undoing the operator's manual fail in exactly the stuck-running cases this button is meant to handle.
  </results>
  </user_action>

<user_action>
  <context>User initiated a review task. Here's the full review output from reviewer model. User may select one or more comments to resolve.</context>
  <action>review</action>
  <results>
  The patch introduces new abort/race regressions in the review startup and recovery flows. These cases can orphan created reviews or overwrite/discard valid completed output, so the change is not correct as written.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Stop aborting once startup has created persistent artifacts — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts:323-332
  If the Studio SSE client disconnects after `resolveReviewContext()` has already created the workspace/deployment, `emitEvent()` here still throws `AbortError` and the start flow exits before any review is attached to those artifacts. In auto mode the later abort check before `approveReviewPolicy()` has the same problem after `deriveReviewPolicy()` succeeds, leaving an orphaned `policy_ready` review with no returned `reviewId`. After startup has begun mutating backend state, disconnects should stop streaming only, not cancel the handoff.

- [P1] Fence manual fail against concurrent completion — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts:297-302
  This update is unconditional after the initial `getReviewRun()` read. If a running review finishes between that read and this write, the endpoint will clear the fresh report and downgrade the review to `failed/review_execution_aborted`; a queued→running race similarly returns success even though the fail did not actually apply. The manual-fail path needs a compare-and-swap on the observed status (and attempt for `running`) so a late click cannot destroy completed output.

- [P2] Accept successful completion after a retry requeues the same attempt — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts:27-29
  Recovery can move a stale `running` review back to `queued` with `retry_scheduled` while the original attempt is still executing. If that original attempt finishes before the replacement worker claims the queue, this new `latest.status !== 'running'` guard drops the successful report on the floor, so the review remains queued and users wait for an unnecessary second pass—or never see the success if the retry never runs. The finalizer needs to allow the same-attempt `queued/retry_scheduled` state to persist success.
  </results>
  </user_action>

findings.title: [P1] Stop aborting once startup has created persistent artifacts
findings.body: If the Studio SSE client disconnects after `resolveReviewContext()` has already created the workspace/deployment, `emitEvent()` here still throws `AbortError` and the start flow exits before any review is attached to those artifacts. In auto mode the later abort check before `approveReviewPolicy()` has the same problem after `deriveReviewPolicy()` succeeds, leaving an orphaned `policy_ready` review with no returned `reviewId`. After startup has begun mutating backend state, disconnects should stop streaming only, not cancel the handoff.

findings.title: [P1] Fence manual fail against concurrent completion
findings.body: This update is unconditional after the initial `getReviewRun()` read. If a running review finishes between that read and this write, the endpoint will clear the fresh report and downgrade the review to `failed/review_execution_aborted`; a queued→running race similarly returns success even though the fail did not actually apply. The manual-fail path needs a compare-and-swap on the observed status (and attempt for `running`) so a late click cannot destroy completed output.

findings.title: [P2] Accept successful completion after a retry requeues the same attempt
findings.body: Recovery can move a stale `running` review back to `queued` with `retry_scheduled` while the original attempt is still executing. If that original attempt finishes before the replacement worker claims the queue, this new `latest.status !== 'running'` guard drops the successful report on the floor, so the review remains queued and users wait for an unnecessary second pass—or never see the success if the retry never runs. The finalizer needs to allow the same-attempt `queued/retry_scheduled` state to persist success.

In auto mode the later abort check before `approveReviewPolicy()` has the same problem after `deriveReviewPolicy()` succeeds, leaving an orphaned `policy_ready` review with no returned `reviewId`. After startup has begun mutating backend state, disconnects should stop streaming only, not cancel the handoff.

- [P1] Fence manual fail against concurrent completion — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts:297-302
  This update is unconditional after the initial `getReviewRun()` read. If a running review finishes between that read and this write, the endpoint will clear the fresh report and downgrade the review to `failed/review_execution_aborted`; a queued→running race similarly returns success even though the fail did not actually apply. The manual-fail path needs a compare-and-swap on the observed status (and attempt for `running`) so a late click cannot destroy completed output.

- [P2] Accept successful completion after a retry requeues the same attempt — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts:27-29
  Recovery can move a stale `running` review back to `queued` with `retry_scheduled` while the original attempt is still executing. If that original attempt finishes before the replacement worker claims the queue, this new `latest.status !== 'running'` guard drops the successful report on the floor, so the review remains queued and users wait for an unnecessary second pass—or never see the success if the retry never runs. The finalizer needs to allow the same-attempt `queued/retry_scheduled` state to persist success.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. payload.message:
Found:
- The fail-review toast finding was real. [`ReportPage.tsx`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/components/ReportPage.tsx) always showed “Review marked failed” on any 2xx `/fail` response, even when the returned review had already ended in a different status.
- The startup-abort finding was real in the SSE proxy path. [`ui-proxy.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/ui-proxy.ts) was still aborting `startStudioNewReview()` on socket close, even though workspace/deployment setup is not actually cancellable once started.

Fixed:
- I changed [`ReportPage.tsx`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/report-ui/src/components/ReportPage.tsx) to base the toast on the returned review status. It now shows `Review marked failed` only when the review actually ends up `failed`; otherwise it reports the returned terminal state.
- I removed disconnect-driven abort propagation from the Studio SSE proxy in [`ui-proxy.ts`](/Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/ui-proxy.ts). Closing the stream now stops streaming only; it no longer cancels the backend startup handoff mid-flight.

  <results>
  The patch adds useful recovery hardening, but it also introduces incorrect terminal-state handling for recovered and manually failed runs, plus a startup abort path that can strand created reviews. The new evidence gate can also make some review analyses fail despite valid output.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Preserve late success after stale-review recovery requeues work — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts:27-29
  When `recoverStaleRunningReviewIfNeeded()` moves a timed-out run back to `queued` with `retry_scheduled`, the original attempt is still allowed to keep running. If that in-flight attempt finishes successfully before the replacement claim starts, `finalizeSuccessfulReview()` now drops the valid report because the status is no longer `running`, so the review is re-run unnecessarily and can stay queued even though a correct result was already available.

- [P1] Fence manual fail against the still-running attempt — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts:297-302
  For `running` reviews, this new `/fail` path only flips the row to `failed`; it does not cancel or fence the active worker. The unchanged runner paths in `packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner.ts` and `.../retry.ts` can still schedule a retry or write a different terminal failure when that original attempt finally exits, so a user who manually fails a stuck run can watch it come back as `queued` or lose the manual-fail error.

- [P2] Finish review startup after a client disconnects — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/studio-create.ts:393-394
  In the SSE start flow, `ui-proxy.ts` now aborts `startStudioNewReview()` as soon as the browser connection closes, but this function still honors that abort even after `deriveReviewPolicy()` has already created the review. In auto mode, an abort between review creation and `approveReviewPolicy()` will leave a hidden, never-queued review behind; in review mode the same disconnect can create a policy review that is never returned to the caller.

- [P2] Only require cross-file reads when search found cross-file evidence — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-analysis.ts:300-301
  `extractIntegrationSearchQueries()` now turns many UI/API diffs into `requiresCrossFileEvidence=true`, but this guard requires a non-changed file read even when `search_code` only matched changed files or found nothing. In those cases the review loop has no way to satisfy the requirement, so otherwise valid analyses are rejected with `review_analysis_insufficient_evidence` or run out of steps for self-contained diffs that merely mention an integration symbol like `onEvent` or `/recover`.

content.text: are we running in cirlces here with thse code reviews? Are these reviews reaching dimishing returns or is it worth it to keep running them?

payload.message: are we running in cirlces here with thse code reviews? Are these reviews reaching dimishing returns or is it worth it to keep running them?

Yes, you’re hitting diminishing returns.

What I’m seeing is:
- The reviewer is still finding some real issues, but the hit rate has dropped.
- A growing share of the comments are stale or are re-reporting bugs that are already fixed in the current tree.
- We’re spending more time verifying reviewer drift than fixing new defects.

That usually means the review loop is no longer the highest-leverage tool for this patch set. The value now is probably:
- Catching one last real race or contract bug if it exists.
- Converting the real classes of bugs you already found into regression tests.
- Stopping once consecutive review runs are mostly stale/noisy.

My recommendation:
- Do not keep running reviews indefinitely on the same patch stack.
- Run at most one more review pass after the latest fixes.
- If that pass is mostly stale again, stop and shift to targeted regression tests plus a normal final sanity pass.

The practical bar I’d use:
- If the next review has 0-1 real findings and the rest are stale, you’re done.
- If it finds another truly new P1/P2, fix it and run one final confirmation pass.
- If repeated runs keep surfacing the same already-fixed themes, the reviewer has started to lag the code and you should stop trusting iterative reruns as the main signal.

So: yes, you are starting to go in circles. One final pass is reasonable; beyond that, it’s probably wasted time unless the next run surfaces a clearly new bug.

  <results>
  The patch introduces at least two state-management regressions in review recovery/finalization, and the new SSE abort wiring can cancel startup after partial setup work. Those issues can lose valid review results or make the new fail/start flows unreliable.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Allow stale-recovered attempts to finalize successfully — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/lib/review-runner/finalization.ts:27-29
  When `handleGetReview()` auto-recovers a stale running review, `recoverStaleRunningReviewIfNeeded()` moves it to `queued` with `error_code='retry_scheduled'` before the original worker is fenced. If that original attempt finishes successfully a moment later, this new guard drops the report because the row is no longer `running`, so the valid result is lost and the queued retry proceeds anyway.

- [P1] Fence manual fail against later retry scheduling — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/worker/src/api/reviews/recovery.ts:297-302
  This new running-state fail path only flips the review row to `failed`. The worker loop still calls `scheduleReviewRetry()` on later transient errors without checking for `review_execution_aborted`, so a user who clicks “Fail review” on a stuck run can have it bounce back to `queued` as soon as the in-flight attempt later hits a retryable provider/db/network failure. Manual fail needs to fence or abort the current attempt before it can reschedule itself.

- [P2] Don't cancel startup when the SSE client disconnects — /Users/nickdejesus/Code/nimbus/packages/cli/src/app/reviews/ui-proxy.ts:196-199
  Aborting the `/start/events` flow on `response.close` now feeds an `AbortSignal` into `startStudioNewReview()`, and `resolveReviewContext()` treats that as fatal before review creation. If the browser tab is closed or the SSE drops during checkpoint/workspace/deployment setup, the flow exits with `AbortError` after some setup work has already succeeded, but before a review ID exists, leaving unattached startup artifacts and forcing the user to rerun the whole start flow.
